claim: Through a held hub, emergence composes as a 2-sum. Let a knot space have a simple 3-edge cut with point side P (ports p1, p2, p3) and line side Q, and remove a line M that does not lie in P. (1) The hub holds: on every remaining solution the ports take two complementary all-equal patterns, so they carry one binary value h. (2) The solutions are the join of their P-part and their (Q plus ports)-part along h, and both parts are closed under complementing every value, which flips h; so for every set X of non-port variables the two halves of its projection (h = 0, h = 1) have equal size. (3) Hence a set X u Y, with X in P minus the ports and Y in Q both nonempty, is a circuit of the solutions exactly when X u {p} is a circuit of the P-part and Y u {p} a circuit of the other part, for a port p (any port, since they are tied); and no circuit meeting both P's interior and Q contains a port. The crossing knots are the 2-sum of the two sides' circuits through the hub, ties included: cycle-like composition at the hub that selection leaves. (4) Without complement symmetry this fails: two circuits through a bit, each deficient at one value only, eliminate to a free set. Checked by brute force on every splice of two census knot spaces up to 13 points (one line and point each), at every removal off the point side: the crossing circuits equal the predicted 2-sum exactly.
